technology_name: Gravity Compensation Hydraulic Damper for Postural Transients
constitutional_basis: Article LII (falsification contract). This contract LIFTS the R339-recorded protocol into the 12-element directive schema — the recorded protocol (mock CSF loop, 3 arms, 4 pressures, 10 runs, blinded) is the historical basis, quoted not replaced.
question: What is the cheapest credible way to learn whether this technology deserves more money?
hypothesis: Across the physiological postural pressure set, the hydraulic damper beats the ASD baseline on the two pre-declared unestablished differentiators — response time to a postural pressure step and proportional (continuous) modulation of flow — by margins that are clinically material, while matching or improving the ASD's target-flow accuracy.
null_hypothesis: The damper does not beat the ASD on either pre-declared endpoint by a clinically material margin (including: response-time differences vanish at physiological transition rates; proportional behavior produces no measurable flow-smoothing benefit vs the ASD's action), OR the damper's target-flow accuracy is materially WORSE than the ASD's (already modeled: ASD is closer to target in 3/4 postures).
control: TWO control arms on the identical bench loop (Constitution Art. XLVII — baseline unchanged across arms, identical instrument): (1) ASD (anti-siphon device) — the incumbent real baseline architecture the differentiators are claimed against; (2) standard valve catheter — the null baseline.
treatment: The damper element (annular-gap architecture, shipped 0.18 mm gap class) inline in the same mock CSF loop.
apparatus: Mock CSF loop (R339-recorded protocol): pressure-head reservoir programmable across 10/20/30/40 mmHg postural pressures, flow sensor, postural-step actuation (step transition profile representative of the 1-3 s physiological transition recorded in the differentiation audit), blinded analysis harness.
inputs: 3 arms x 4 postural pressures x 10 runs each (the recorded protocol); postural step profiles (pre-registered transition rates: physiological 1-3 s class AND a fast-step stress case); fluid at controlled temperature.
outputs: Per run: flow response time to the postural step; flow-trace smoothness/proportionality metrics (the two primary endpoints, matching the declared differentiators: response_time_damper_ms, proportional_error_pct — the R346-recorded endpoint names); steady-state flow vs target per posture; under-drainage/over-drainage excursions.
measurement_method: Continuous flow + pressure acquisition; response-time and proportionality metrics computed by a pre-registered analysis script; blinded analysis (recorded protocol requirement).
baseline: The ASD arm's performance on the same endpoints (and the standard arm as the null anchor) — the R339 comparison table is the MODELLED prior; the bench delivers the measured successor.
primary_endpoint: Response time to postural pressure step (damper vs ASD) AND proportional flow modulation error (damper vs ASD) — the two unestablished differentiators promoted to endpoints by the R339 g3 decision.
secondary_endpoints: Target-flow matching across the 4 postural pressures (the modeled weakness: ASD closer in 3/4 — does the bench confirm?)
Settling behavior vs the first-order model (tau = I_h/c_h) — model-vs-bench residual
acceptance_threshold: ACCEPT only if: the damper beats ASD on BOTH primary endpoints by the pre-registered margins AND target-flow accuracy is not materially worse than ASD. The margins must be pre-registered from clinical materiality argument (owner-gated: the differentiation audit records that materiality evidence is currently NONE — deriving the clinically material margin is part of this protocol's pre-registration, Constitution Art. XXVII BUYER_DEFINED/CLINICAL class, never modelled-number silently promoted).
falsifier: KILL (per the R339-recorded decision rule) if the bench shows neither differentiator is clinically material: response-speed advantage vanishes at physiological transition rates AND proportional behavior shows no measurable flow benefit — then the package enters the repair pipeline; if repair fails, cemetery. A materially worse target-flow accuracy than ASD is a DISADVANTAGE-class negative (already modeled 3/4) that alone justifies rejection unless a differentiator is decisively positive.
uncertainty: Mock loop fluid is water/CSF-mimic (viscosity anchored to the NIST 310.15 K class; CSF residual disclosed); mock loop excludes biological fouling and in-vivo compliance; clinical materiality margins currently unargued (owner-gated); the ASD arm's commercial device tolerances may differ from the modeled ASD profile (use a real ASD device, not a model, per directive section 10 'compare against a real baseline architecture').
sample_size_basis: 3 arms x 4 pressures x 10 runs (the recorded R339 protocol) — sized to detect the modeled effect classes; a power analysis for the materiality margins is part of pre-registration (owner-gated).
cost_basis: $15K (recorded in PORTFOLIO_COMMERCIAL_STATE.json / R339 buyer package for this exact protocol class).
decision_rule: ACCEPT -> SPONSORED_VALIDATION with the first PHYSICAL_OBSERVATION-class evidence for this package (response time + proportional modulation, measured vs a real ASD) attached through the reality-boundary interface. KILL -> repair pipeline then cemetery (the R339-recorded path), with the lesson codified (Constitution Art. LI). MIXED (one differentiator positive, one null) -> recorded exactly so; no partial promotion.
prior_state: The R339 buyer package records the decisive experiment (question 'Does the damper beat ASD on the pre-declared endpoints?'; protocol 'Mock CSF loop, damper vs ASD vs standard, 4 postural pressures (10/20/30/40 mmHg), 10 runs each, blinded analysis'; pass/fail rules quoted; $15K/8 weeks). This contract is the schema-compliant versioned lift of that recorded protocol, not a new invention.
